**The economy (Stage 2).** From Town (150 people) the city grows past House: Townhouses want pottery, and four Townhouses or empty plots in a square on a pleasant street join into a Manor, then a Fine manor (beer and two foods), a Villa (linen) and an Estate (jewellery). Each good has a chain: a clay pit, barley farm, flax farm or gem mine fills a **storehouse**, a workshop next to it turns the raw good into pottery, beer, linen or jewellery, and bazaars sell everything homes use. A storehouse's sheet lets you accept or refuse each good. **Desirability** decides which streets can hold the big homes: gardens, statues, temples and booths make a street nicer, workshops and storage make it worse; placing a building tints the ground it would change and the confirm bar says how many homes it makes nicer or less pleasant, and a home's sheet shows its score and the three biggest causes. The **booth** brings entertainment. At Market town a **trading post** opens trade with Memphis (and Byblos at Great city): for each good choose buy, sell or ignore and a level to keep, and a caravan comes every three months. Milestones run up to Capital (1,000 people); new build cards wear a "New" badge, and the next milestone's cards show greyed with when they unlock. Overlays add goods, entertainment and desirability. **Difficulty** (Relaxed, Normal, Hard, chosen under New city) changes what buildings, roads and trade routes cost.

```markdown
**The economy (Stage 2).** From Town (150 people) the city grows past House: Townhouses want pottery, and four Townhouses or empty plots in a square on a pleasant street join into a Manor, then a Fine manor (beer and two foods), a Villa (linen) and an Estate (jewellery). Each good has a chain: a clay pit, barley farm, flax farm or gem mine fills a **storehouse**, a workshop next to it turns the raw good into pottery, beer, linen or jewellery, and bazaars sell everything homes use. A storehouse's sheet lets you accept or refuse each good. **Desirability** decides which streets can hold the big homes: gardens, statues, temples and booths make a street nicer, workshops and storage make it worse; placing a building tints the ground it would change and the confirm bar says how many homes it makes nicer or less pleasant, and a home's sheet shows its score and the three biggest causes. The **booth** brings entertainment. At Market town a **trading post** opens trade with Memphis (and Byblos at Great city): for each good choose buy, sell or ignore and a level to keep, and a caravan comes every three months. Milestones run up to Capital (1,000 people); new build cards wear a "New" badge, and the next milestone's cards show greyed with when they unlock. Overlays add goods, entertainment and desirability. **Difficulty** (Peaceful, Relaxed, Normal, Hard, chosen under New city) changes what buildings, roads and trade routes cost, and from Stage 3 how fast fire risk builds and how big raids are; Peaceful has no raids.

**Danger (Stage 3).** From Town, buildings build up fire risk (workshops fastest, homes slowly). A **firehouse** (Services, from Village) cuts the build-up of every building within 8 road tiles and puts out a blaze there in a day or two; a blaze no staffed firehouse reaches grows into a fire after three days, burns for 10 to 15 days and can spread to its neighbours. A burned home leaves empty plots and its people leave; anything else leaves rubble, which costs gold to clear with Demolish. The fire-risk overlay (O) shows where it builds. From 250 people raiders come: the first warning appears two game-years later, three months before they arrive, with a countdown, the direction they come from and what they are after; **Pay tribute** buys off any raid but the first, and the raid report afterwards shows what your defences stopped. At Market town the Defence cards open: **walls** (drawn like roads; wall over a road makes a gate), **towers** (they shoot raiders within 4 tiles) and **barracks** (up to four soldiers, 8 gold a month each, in peace too). Raiders burn and steal but never hurt anyone, and a raid is beaten once half of them fall. A working temple can hold a **festival** once a year from Town (+6 mood for three months). A fire or a raid raises a banner; the **On a fire** setting chooses what the game does after the first one (Just tell me, Go to it, or Pause).

**Score (Stage 3).** The city summary scores the city in four parts (People, Prosperity, Culture and Safety, 0 to 100 each), each with its main reason, times the difficulty's factor (Peaceful 0.7, Relaxed 0.8, Normal 1, Hard 1.25); the parts' total earns bronze, silver or gold at 160, 240 and 320. **Seal this reign** keeps the score as a stamp on the title card, which lists your three best scores; **Share score** makes a link and a picture card (friends' honour, nothing is checked), and **This week's Nile** on the title card is a seed everyone gets for the week. **Screenshot mode** (☰ menu) hides the interface until the next tap. The opening adds Founded Thebes, ten feats to chase, and citizens' remarks; from Capital a bar shows the points to the next medal. **Ambient life** (river glints, swaying reeds and trees, smoke, the odd bird or boat) runs on the real clock; Settings → Ambient motion turns it off, and reduced motion stops it.
```

Create `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-10-11-stage-3-followups.md`:

```markdown
# Stage 3 follow-ups

Things the Stage 3 integration (Track F) found or left open. None blocks the stage; each says what it costs if left.

## Balance

- **The band is met without tuning a number.** The 10-year village (`tests/sim/longrun.test.js`) spends 65.3% of its taxes on wages, upkeep and soldiers' pay once it has two firehouses and three towers, against 45% without them (ruling 114's 60-70%). It uses towers, not a barracks, so the band does not depend on how many soldiers are in training. The capital run spends 39% with five firehouses, two barracks and two towers (eight soldiers), so the late game stays generous until Stage 4's monuments, as ruling 114 expected.
- **Measured with Tracks A and B:** the village meets 26 blazes in ten years, all put out, nothing burned, and three raids (3 to 6 raiders), all beaten by its towers; the capital run meets 27 blazes, all put out, and two raids (the second of 12), both beaten. The long runs assert no raid lost and at most six buildings burned, so a retune of fire or combat has some room.

## Fire

- **A home with no road beside it can never be covered.** `fireCoverage` reads a building's road tiles, so the second row of homes behind a street (the capital run's row 14, any home deep in a block) builds risk at the full rate and burns sooner or later, whatever the player builds. Cost if left: blocks of homes burn from the inside. A fix: let a home take the best coverage of a covered neighbour, or of any road tile within 2 tiles.
- **Firehouses take workers before temples and bazaars** (`safety` comes before `services` in `PRIORITY_LEVELS`). A Town of 150 people has about 60 workers, and eight firehouses (the sample city's) want 32 of them before any temple or bazaar gets one. Cost if left: a player who builds several firehouses early sees homes lose their temple or bazaar. A fix: rank the firehouse with services, or give it 2 workers.

## Fixtures and tools

- **The seed-7 sample city is poorer.** Its nine firehouses cost 180 gold a month; at day 600 it has -1,347 gold (Stage 2: -425). The default early-game shots (`tools/shots.ps1`, seed 7) then show the well refused below the debt floor in the placing scene. A fix: move those scenes to seed 11, as the Stage 2 and Stage 3 sets are.
- **The stress city has no walls.** Its grid of roads and homes leaves no free line for `drawWall`, so the wall layer's frame cost at 64 x 64 is not measured. A fix: leave a free band in the stress city and draw a ring around a district.
- **`devScene` writes the contract's state directly** (`b.fire`, `raid.warning`, `raid.active`, soldiers, wall tiles; `src/dev/scenes.js`). If a track adds a required field to one of those records, the scenes need it too. The battle scene extends the sample city's north road three tiles to make its gate.
- **The title backdrop** builds in about 70 ms on a laptop with fire and raids running (the same as Stage 2's), so it is neither precomputed nor shortened; a phone takes a few times longer. `tests/stage3/balance/cities.test.js` fails it at a second.

## Words

- **Peaceful's hint** names no raids, the slower fire risk and the Relaxed prices, but not its score factor (0.7) or the goals, feats and achievements it skips. Cost if left: a player learns those from the summary.
- **The summary's order** puts Track D's last raid report before Track E's score section (both tracks' contract notes); `devScene('score')` scrolls to `.score-section` either way. Swapping the two entries of `parts` in `createUI.js` puts the score first, as the contract's prose had it.
```
